cohort: All women who gave birth in a rural mission hospital in Malawi between 2015 and 2016.
finding: Prolonged second stage of labour was relatively common (9.0%) and associated with an increased risk of maternal complications, particularly postpartum haemorrhage, though there was no difference in neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Among women with prolonged second stage, 69.0% had spontaneous vaginal births, 20.9% had caesarean sections, and 10.1% had vacuum extractions, with caesarean section occurring twice as often as vacuum extraction.
